audits.title: When Stale Constraints Go Unchecked
audits.published_claim: arXiv:2608.25553v2 reports a fixed two-record verification budget with 1,800 primary, 1,800 fresh-wording replication, 900 held-out and 900 corrected held-out episodes. In stated+superseded cells native current-record-consistent decisions were 34/150, 38/150 and 38/150 in the first three runs; forced-critical was 145/150, 147/150 and 130/150, for +74.0, +72.7 and +61.3 pp. The corrected held-out robustness run was 36/150 vs 146/150, +73.3 pp. The intervention is explicitly an experimenter-known critical-path allocation instrument, not a deployable scheduler.
audits.official_artifact_support: Strong declared support: arXiv v2 metadata explicitly states that manuscript, LaTeX source, all 5,400 episode files, frozen specifications, timestamp proofs and scripts are archived at Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22117197. The paper states the primary/replication/original-heldout specifications were frozen and timestamped before confirmatory execution and the corrected held-out specification was externally deposited before execution.
audits.independent_replication: None protocol-matched found. The paper's fresh-wording and corrected-held-out runs are same-study replications, not third-party independent reproduction.
audits.failed_replication: The original held-out scenario contained a disclosed temporal inconsistency. The authors retained that result unchanged and ran a prospectively specified corrected robustness replication; the corrected run increased the contrast to +73.3 pp. This is a disclosed within-study design defect with successful same-study robustness replication, not an independent failed replication.
audits.missing_dependencies_config: The runtime could not fetch the Zenodo record through available transport, so the auditor did not hash/read or execute the archived scripts and 5,400 episode files in this invocation. Exact model API builds also remain historical hosted dependencies.
audits.o_specific_adaptation: Any deployment rule that automatically routes scarce verification to freshness/supersession paths is downstream adaptation. The published intervention knows the critical path by design.
audits.scope: Exact to the paper's inherited-memory supersession instrument, six named models, two-record budget, fixed scenarios and deterministic outcome definition. Do not generalize +61–74 pp to arbitrary memory systems, retrieval budgets, stale facts, or schedulers.

audits.title: Self-evolution capability/security drift in AgentDojo Banking
audits.published_claim: arXiv:2608.17684v1 reports a corrected 15-family AgentDojo Banking v1.2.2 audit. On Qwen3.7-Flash, SkillOpt changes utility 0.741->0.837, exposure 0.820->0.943, conditional ASR 0.605->0.562, total ASR 0.496->0.530 and unauthorized financial-state change 0.583->0.685. Capability, exposure and unauthorized-state deltas are positive in all three independently evolved lineages; total-ASR delta is positive in only two of three. The paper explicitly treats the comparison as end-to-end and does not attribute differences to representation alone.
audits.official_artifact_support: Paper-level protocol detail is strong: byte-identical acquisition records within each lineage, sealed endpoint variants, family-level repeated-measurement accounting, checker audit, fixed model/config and exact lineage deltas are reported. However the paper explicitly says code and audit artifacts will be released upon publication; they are not currently released in the arXiv artifact, and no intended public repository was found.
audits.independent_replication: None protocol-matched found. The three lineages are independent end-to-end repetitions within the same study, not external replication.
audits.failed_replication: The pooled total-ASR increase is not directionally replicated in all lineages: one lineage is -7.4 pp while the others are +7.3 and +10.4 pp. The worker correctly preserves this as a boundary rather than claiming uniform ASR worsening.
audits.missing_dependencies_config: No released code/audit bundle/raw trajectories or immutable hosted-model snapshot. Five provider-side repetition-guardrail rejections are disclosed for the SkillOpt attacked endpoint.
audits.o_specific_adaptation: Using separate capability/exposure/conditional-susceptibility/unauthorized-effect acceptance gates in another controller is downstream adaptation; the measured decomposition itself is published.
audits.scope: One simulated e-banking suite, one primary executor, one attack family and three lineages. End-to-end methods differ jointly in write eligibility, admission, update, state representation and retrieval; do not infer a representation-only or universal self-evolution safety effect.

audits.title: AWM execution-interface mismatch
audits.published_claim: In the same arXiv:2608.17684 study, AWM-LiteralPort has utility 0.319, exposure 0.299, ASR 0.195 and unauthorized-state 0.217. Exactly 380/540 rollouts emit a textual <action> block and the same 380 execute zero real tools. A post-hoc interface arm reuses the same three workflows, removes only four literal tag types while preserving all non-tag bytes, and changes utility to 0.756, exposure to 0.909, ASR to 0.575, unauthorized-state to 0.714, with zero-tool rate 0.704->0.046.
audits.official_artifact_support: The paper reports thirty pre-run content-equivalence assertions for the post-hoc arm and exact diagnostic counts. But code and audit artifacts are explicitly deferred until publication, so the claimed byte-preservation and 380/540 identity cannot be independently checked from released raw artifacts in this invocation.
audits.failed_replication: None; the post-hoc arm is a sensitivity diagnosis, not a preregistered primary replication.
audits.missing_dependencies_config: No released frozen workflows, raw rollouts, executor code or immutable hosted-model snapshot.
audits.o_specific_adaptation: Requiring artifact-executor compatibility tests before accepting safety/utility numbers is downstream evaluation policy; the specific AWM diagnostic is a published post-hoc result.
audits.scope: This diagnoses one literal WebArena-style action envelope in one native function-calling executor. It does not establish that AWM generally suppresses tools or that interface adaptation always raises attack success.

audits.title: The Framing Gap
audits.published_claim: arXiv:2608.27092v1 reports a safe synthetic canary/mock-tool lab. On gpt-4o, ten overt injection classes reach 0% while selected reframings reach 100%; pooled reframing is 40.0% in the main gpt-4o table. Removing the confidentiality policy changes a same-run reframing comparison 31.9%->38.1% with base remaining 0%. A destination allow-list and a planner/reader capability split reach 0% under their tested conditions; SecAlign is 32.5% and channel separation 38.8% in a separate common Llama-3.1-8B harness. A normalizing guard is 0% on anticipated encodings but ROT13, held out from that canonicalizer, leaks 100% in its row.
audits.official_artifact_support: Full arXiv HTML gives trial counts, matched clean-vs-poisoned scoring, defense harness distinctions, run-to-run variance caveats and positive control for SecAlign. No public code/data repository or release link was found in the paper or GitHub repository search.
audits.independent_replication: None protocol-matched found. Cross-model reruns and the no-policy ablation are within-study experiments.
audits.failed_replication: The paper itself cautions against fine ordering among surface defenses because single-run spread is within documented run-to-run swing. Mistral is a stated cross-model exception with only a 1.5-point framing shift. These are scope boundaries, not family-wide failures.
audits.missing_dependencies_config: No released raw prompts/trials, runner, seeds/API snapshots or code artifact found.
audits.o_specific_adaptation: A generic downstream rule favoring payload-blind destination/capability controls is an adaptation. The paper's 0% values are empirical results in its mock environment, not proofs for arbitrary deployed destinations or planner/reader architectures.
audits.scope: Synthetic canary secret, mock tools, selected wordings/models, two distinct inference scaffolds for different defense tables. Do not compare absolute rates across those scaffolds or generalize tested 0% cells to arbitrary encodings/destinations.

audits.title: REDAgentBench measurement-view and evaluation-cue sensitivity
audits.published_claim: arXiv:2608.10669v1 reports 1,661 executable cases across five service surfaces. For RQ2 it holds each rollout and Qwen3.7-plus judge backbone fixed over 401 matched task-harness slots per model while varying the complete view-specific judging configuration. State-judge ASR is 7.73–11.72 pp higher than trajectory-judge ASR for all six tested models, with 12.97–21.20% paired label changes and all six exact McNemar p<=6.54e-5. Evaluation-context disclosure lowers ASR 6.59 pp for Qwen3.7-plus and 4.77 pp for Qwen3.5-plus using paired case-clustered intervals, while OpenClaw/T4 reverses direction. In 2,846 resolved state-confirmed Qwen-plus harmful executions, broad recognition is 17.92% and strict recognition 5.48%. A selected 510-case Qwen-plus policy-reminder replay reduces ASR 74.19 pp with source-case-cluster CI [69.85,78.41].
audits.official_artifact_support: The paper provides detailed construction, deterministic receipt/state verification design, matched judging protocol, case-cluster statistical treatment and supplementary-material descriptions. No benchmark code/data repository or release link was found in the paper or GitHub repository search; arXiv metadata only notes supplementary material included.
audits.failed_replication: Evaluation-disclosure effect is explicitly nonuniform: OpenClaw/T4 moves +6.02 and +4.82 pp for the two models. The reminder result is a selected harmful-case replay and does not estimate full-benchmark ASR.
audits.missing_dependencies_config: No released 1,661-case bundle, rollouts/receipts, view-specific judge prompts/gates as runnable files, model/API snapshots or full runner found.
audits.o_specific_adaptation: Requiring the full (harness, judging configuration, evaluation cue, judge backbone) tuple in downstream safety certificates is a policy adaptation directly motivated by the paper; it is not itself an externally replicated standard.
audits.scope: View sensitivity is the paper's six-model fixed-rollout audit; cue sensitivity is two Qwen-plus models; recognition is a Qwen-plus diagnostic cohort; reminder effectiveness is selected replay cohorts. Do not generalize any one effect magnitude to every model, harness or benchmark cue.

The archive itself was not transport-readable in this invocation, so auditor execution replay remains incomplete.

FE-356 pooled ASR worsening is not directionally consistent across all three lineages.

FE-358 empirical 0% defenses remain mock-lab/tested-configuration results, not universal proofs.
